messages:
ravi: quick sync notes: thinking about admission quotas vs demotion tokens for fairness. wanted to dump ideas here.

jess: do you mean replace per-request admission tokens with a slower demotion signal? that has pros/cons.

ravi: exactly. admissions are expensive at high qps. demote tokens are cheaper but coarser. maybe combine: tokens for admission during ramp, demote tokens for steady-state adjustments.

noah: performance thought: admission token evals are on-path and add ~300us p50. at 100k rps that's costly. demote tokens as cached policy looks cheaper.

tammy: how do we avoid stale tokens causing unfairness? need versioned tokens and a fallback to local heuristics if token invalid.

infra-bot: perf-test: admission-vs-token-latency: baseline 0.3ms/op with admission, 0.05ms/op with cached token enforcement.

ravi: proposal: 1) use admission tokens for bursts and ramp-up (5m window). 2) after steady detection, central issues demote token that proxies enforce for cool windows. 3) proxies still keep EWMA-based fast sheds.

jess: also need visibility: emit `admission.token_miss` and `demote.token_enforced`. tie to billing to catch over-enforced tenants.

noah: edge case: token revocation on policy rollback. we need revoke list or short TTLs. prefer short TTL + sequence id to avoid heavy revoke infra.

ravi: short TTL + sequence id + signed token seems fine. default TTL 5m. On rollback central increments seq so tokens expire quickly.

tammy: can we simulate token storms where many tenants get reissued? load tests should include token issuance QPS.

infra-bot: added simulation job `fair.tokens.storm` to CI queue.

ravi: next steps: jess to spec telemetry and billing tie-in; noah to prototype token cache in proxy; tammy to add token revocation sim; i'll write a short RFC appendix.

jess: rolling to experimental non-prod region first. watch `admission.latency` and `demote.token_enforced` metrics.

noah: I'll open PR `proxy: add token cache + validation` with feature flag.

ravi: end.
